toposort_diamond.detail: every edge (u,v) must have pos(u) < pos(v)

toposort_vs_networkx.detail: both orderings must be topologically valid (not necessarily identical)

dijkstra_01_3.detail: shortest path 0->1->3 has length 2; 0->3 direct is 4

acyclic_detection_positive.detail: diamond DAG must register as acyclic

witness_shell_nesting_dag.detail: Replays the shell-nesting DAG operations (PyDiGraph, topological_sort, dag_longest_path_length, is_directed_acyclic_graph) used load-bearingly in the witness sim.

toposort_on_cycle_raises.detail: rustworkx must refuse to linearize a cycle

ill_formed_edge_raises.detail: edge to undefined node must raise

empty_graph_acyclic.detail: empty graph is vacuously acyclic with empty topo order

perf_vs_networkx_1k.detail: Both orderings must be valid; speedup reported for context, not load-bearing.

surviving_alternatives: This receipt covers only bounded rustworkx graph-ordering capability; it does not promote graph-shell geometry, dependency collapse, bridge, axis, GStack, or nonclassical admission.
demotion_condition: Demote this rustworkx capability receipt if DAG topological ordering, transitive reduction, Dijkstra distance, cycle rejection, witness shell DAG, or boundary graph controls fail on rerun.
claim_ceiling: finite sim_rustworkx_capability lego receipt only; no bridge, GStack, axis, QIT, or nonclassical admission
next_lego_target: Use as bounded rustworkx graph-ordering capability evidence before exact graph lego-fit or coupling packets.
promotion_condition: Requires separate coupling/coexistence receipts and explicit stage-gate approval.
blocked_until: explicit coupling-stage admission and companion receipts
